reasons.C: Present-tense genial irony with epigrammatic turns and period diction; its sentence rhythm and dry, amused stance sit closest to the passage without overdoing it.
reasons.A: Period register and ironic stance fit, but the shift to past tense and the frequent first-person asides make it more reminiscent and essayistic than the passage's present-tense sketch.
reasons.B: Plain modern diction ('in on', 'funnier') and flat, even sentences with little wit; the stance is explanatory, not the author's playful irony.
